title: In 1945, a Woman Fell 75 Floors in an Elevator and Lived

scenes.text: In 1945, a woman fell 75 floors in an elevator. And lived.
Thick fog. A B-25 bomber slams into the Empire State Building at the 79th floor.
One engine drops down an elevator shaft and cuts the cables.
Betty Lou Oliver is inside. The car falls 1,000 feet to the basement.
The severed cables pile up underneath, and trapped air slows the car like a cushion.
Broken back, neck and pelvis. She walked out of hospital. Still the longest elevator fall ever survived.
scenes.keywords: New York skyline Empire State Building

description:
On 28 July 1945, a B-25 bomber lost in fog crashed into the Empire State Building between the 78th and 80th floors, killing 14 people.
One engine severed the elevator cables, and operator Betty Lou Oliver plunged about 1,000 feet, 75 storeys, to the basement. The piled-up cables and air pressure in the shaft cushioned the car. She survived with a broken back, neck and pelvis, and holds the record for the longest fall survived in a lift.
Would you ever ride that elevator again? Comment below.
first_comment: The building reopened for business less than 48 hours later. The fire on the 79th floor was out in 40 minutes. What's the highest floor you've ever worked on?
